picks.blurb: TCU vs Texas Tech Score Predictions From the KillerFrogs Staff Skip to main content SI.COM Frogs in the Pros FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM FROGS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM FROGS BB MEM'RIES SWEET TCU was unable to capture a win in its home finale against #2 Utah, losing 38-17. However, the Horned Frogs will get one more shot at becoming bowl-eligible on Thanksgiving Day against the No. 9-ranked Texas Tech Red Raiders. With Sonny Dykes no longer serving as the head coach of the Frogs, interim head coach Andy Avalos will be tasked with attempting to upset Texas Tech in Lubbock. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. CT on ESPN. The Horned Frogs enter the game at 5-6 overall and 3-5 in the Big 12. Texas Tech is 10-1 and 7-1 in conference play. If TCU pulls off the big upset on Thursday, they will become bowl-eligible. Otherwise, the Frogs' season will be over. Either way, the Frogs will have changes coming their way. Texas Tech had a narrow win last week, as Baylor took the Red Raiders to the wire before they came out on top, 20-10. If the Frogs can make Texas Tech QB Thomas Castellanos uncomfortable like Baylor did, I like the Frogs' odds. Texas Tech has also struggled with consistency this season. However, the Frogs will have their hands full if they let him dictate where the ball goes. As I wrote in my Utah report card , the Frogs have quite a bit to fix, but I truly believe they will be playing hard for Andy Avalos in the regular-season finale. Can the Horned Frogs protect the football, play hard, and bring the energy? Here’s how the KillerFrogs staff sees the regular-season finale. Michael Bara V believes the rivalry and the interim coaching change will bring out something special in the Frogs. He expects the defense to rally behind Andy Avalos and help TCU pull off the upset. Aiden Reed sees TCU eliminating Texas Tech from Big 12 contention, assuming BYU wins, as the Frogs take advantage of having nothing to lose and fighting for bowl eligibility. He also expects TCU to pull off its annual Thanksgiving upset. Baileigh Sheffield expects the Frogs to keep things competitive early, but sees Texas Tech pulling away in the second half for a two-touchdown victory. Jackson James is counting on history repeating itself, pointing to TCU's upset of an in-state rival after its last coaching change in 2021. He believes the Frogs will do it again on Thanksgiving Day in Lubbock. Skyler Gerard expects the Frogs to have some extra fire in their regular-season finale under interim head coach Andy Avalos. He’s counting on the defense to hold up as it has all season and help TCU pull off the upset. As for me, I have been saying all season long that the Frogs would upset Texas Tech, and I'm sticking to that prediction. I believe this team has one more fight left in it, and I expect TCU to rise to the occasion in Andy Avalos' first game as interim head coach. The Red Raiders have the 16th-highest rushing rate in the country, and TCU's defense ranks 18th in yards per rush allowed . The Horned Frogs also have the third-best red-zone defense nationally, which could compound Texas Tech's struggles in high-leverage situations and force the Red Raiders to settle for field goals. Meanwhile, both offensive lines struggle with pass protection and both defenses have high sack rates, opening the door for drive-killing sacks. TCU vs Texas Tech combo I'm essentially investing in Texas Tech winning ugly, which wouldn't be the worst outcome for a team with legitimate College Football Playoff hopes. If TCU can avoid giving the Red Raiders short fields, Texas Tech might have to chew up a significant amount of clock to build a comfortable lead. Furthermore, a two-score deficit wouldn't necessarily force the Horned Frogs to abandon their offensive game plan early, especially if their defense is keeping them within striking distance. picks.blurb: Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Tech couple Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The regular season comes to an end in Galaxy Stadium for the Texas Tech football team , with TCU coming to town for a Thanksgiving showdown under the lights. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. Texas Tech's J'Koby Williams runs with the ball against Arizona State during a Big 12 Conference football game, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. The fired coach theory and TCU TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Of those four other teams switching coaches in season, three of them won their next game, two of them (Baylor and NC State) earning wins of 21 points or more. This theory doesn't always come to fruition, however. During the 2025 coaching cycle, six power-conference programs fired coaches during the season and just one of them won their next game following the axing. That one win came from Virginia Tech, which beat Wofford, so it barely counts. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs TCU Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. away.blurb: Senior quarterback Jaden Craig was initially expected to start and was listed as probable in the first Big 12 player availability report on Wednesday night. TCU head coach Sonny Dykes also said Tuesday that he believed Craig would be able to play. But Craig was downgraded to doubtful in Friday’s injury report and seems unlikely to play against the Utes. Craig was hobbled with an ankle injury during TCU’s 20-10 win over Kanas State last Saturday. Saturday night might mark the start of the Adam Schobel era for TCU football. The sophomore quarterback is expected to earn his first start when the Horned Frogs (5-5, 3-4) host No. 2 Utah (10-0, 7-0) at 8 p.m. Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium on Fox. “I would expect him to play, I think he was a lot better today than he was yesterday,” Dykes said Tuesday. “I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess.” Schobel has played sparingly this season, with just one passing attempt and 11 yards on four carries. But the former four-star recruit is largely viewed as the quarterback of the future for the program. Schobel got his most extensive action of his career in the win over the Wildcats, mostly on designed quarterback runs, but will now be tasked to lead the Horned Frogs against the highest-ranked opponent to play in the Carter since No. 2 Texas in 1970. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. NC State Wolfpack | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation November 25, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football Will Florida State become bowl-eligible for first time since 2023? The Florida State Seminoles will attempt to become bowl-eligible for the first time since 2023 and wrap up their ACC schedule with a .500 record when they host the NC State Wolfpack at Doak Campbell Stadium Saturday afternoon. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on the ACCN. FSU will celebrate its annual Homecoming and Seminole Heritage game and will wear turquoise jerseys and pants for the first time in program history. FSU is 3-0 in Heritage games and 63-12-1 all-time on Homecoming, with 12 consecutive victories. Throughout Native American communities, turquoise represents harmony, friendship and fellowship. The team found out it would wear the jerseys Sunday when defensive back Zae Thomas, a member of the Seminole Tribe of Florida, displayed the uniforms in the team meeting. For more information on FSU’s unique relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida and Seminole Heritage, visit noles.co/Heritage. Florida State football to wear new uniform combination against NC State to honor Seminole Heritage Florida State (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and NC State will meet for the 45th time, with the Noles leading the series, 27-17, including a 16-6 record in Doak. However, NC State has won the last four matchups with Florida State and six of the last seven meetings. Last year, the 11-21 loss at NC State likely cost the 5-win Seminoles the opportunity to become bowl eligible. Under interim head coach Rick Stockstill, the Seminoles will attempt to win their third consecutive game before closing out the season against the Florida Gators at home on Black Friday afternoon, again with another short week to prepare. The last time FSU won 3 straight games was to open the 2025 season before then losing 7 of the next 9 games. The Wolfpack (4-6, 2-5 ACC) also fired their head coach, Dave Doeren, midseason, ending his 14-year tenure as the winningest coach in Wolfpack history, compiling a 98-74 overall record, including 11 bowl appearances and 10 winning seasons. Former NFL quarterback and former Chuck Amato-coached NC State alum, Phillip Rivers, bringing six years’ experience as a Catholic high school football head coach, was officially hired as the new head coach for NC State earlier this week, effective next season. It has been reported that he will travel to Tallahassee along with the Wolfpack team. Rivers signed a reported five-year deal starting at $3.25 million in total compensation for his first year ($2.4375 million base salary plus $812,500 in supplemental income). This is roughly half of Doeren’s previous $6.375 million salary, making Rivers one of the lowest-paid Power 4 coaches. NC State’s interim head coach Todd Goebbel led the team to a 31–10 win over California before suffering a 41–3 blowout loss to Duke and a 34–31 collapse against Syracuse, where the Wolfpack blew an 11-point lead in the final five minutes. Junior 6’6” quarterback CJ Bailey Jr. has completed 186 of his 295 passes attempted for 2,289 yards with 14 TDs and 5 interceptions. Sophomore quarterback Will Wilson, who has only completed 9 of 12 passes for 35 yards, has scored 8 rushing touchdowns for the Wolfpack during his time behind center despite NC State starting seven different lineup combinations on the offensive line in their 10 games due to injuries. Sophomore running back Jayden “Duke” Scott leads the team in rushing with 504 yards on 81 attempts for a 6.22 yard/rush average, along with 5 touchdowns. On defense, linebacker Popo Aguirre leads the team in tackles with 85, followed by CB Brian Nelson II with 47. LB Elijah Satchell leads the team in sacks with five. In their last outing, FSU wrapped up their road schedule with arguably their best defensive performance of the season so far, a 16-10 win at Pittsburgh, under interim defensive coordinator Ernie Sims. FSU’s defense held Pitt, previously ranked 24th in total offense (446), to just 306 total yards, or 140 yards below their season average. The Noles defense allowed only 10 points to the Panthers, 22 points fewer than Pitt’s season average of 31.9 points/game, forced a crucial fourth-and-one turnover on downs in the third quarter, deflected six passes, recorded an interception, and sealed the game with a 4th-down stop on Pitt’s final drive. Florida State’s defense shines in road win over Pitt as Seminoles get back to .500 Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels ranks in the top 20 nationally in six statistical categories: 5th Passing Yards Per Completion 14.61 9th Rushing Touchdowns 13 12th Points Responsible For 166 14th Total Touchdowns 13 15th Points Responsible For Per Game 16.6 16th Yards Per Pass Attempt 8.75 Additionally, Daniels ranks 22nd in the ESPN Total QBR with a 75.7 rating. Florida State vs NCST head-to-head stats comparison FSU kicker Gabe Panikowski is 26-for-26 on field goal attempts in his NCAA career, including 11-for-11 this season. He is the only active kicker (min. 15 attempts) in any NCAA division who is perfect in his career, and his 26 consecutive made field goals at the NCAA level is the longest active streak. Panikowski accounted for 23 points in the two road wins. He became the first FBS player since 2023 with a touchdown, field goal, and 4+ extra points in the win at BC before kicking a season-high three field goals at Pitt. His 47-yarder against Pitt was a season-long. FSU TE Corbyn Fordham is the younger brother of NC State linebacker Caden Fordham, who played against FSU in 2025 and recorded 15 tackles for NC State. NC State was the first team to defeat Florida State at Doak after the Seminoles joined the ACC in 1992. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: NC State Wolfpack-A real toss-up on paper Florida State is currently trending as a 10.5-point favorite with the over/under set at 56.5 points, according to FanDuel. Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. NoleThruandThru (season record: 8-2) FSU may be down 12 running backs but with Ernie Sims’ stare boring holes through opponent foreheads, not even Philip Rivers can save the Pack this time. Give me that sixth win, Stock!!! FSU 23, NC State 17 Tony Morris (season record: 5-0) Homecoming game, beautiful jerseys, gorgeous field. A chance to see Coach Stockstill win a game at home as interim head coach. Gimme the boys in turquoise! FSU 24, NC State 1 4 Seminole Uprising (season record: 7-3) I wish I had time to change my pick from last week after hearing about Pitt’s quarterback change. Oh well. Turning our attention to Saturday, it is hard not to see the Seminoles as a bit of a vibes pick right now. Even though Florida State faced the Panthers’ third-string QB, a road win after a short week will do wonders for this team’s confidence. Meanwhile, NCSU blew another game in ridiculous fashion and is more focused on their new head coach than on the result of this weekend’s game. Injuries are my main concern, but Vegas doesn’t think so, listing the Noles as a 10.5-point favorite. While I do not see a double-digit victory, I do believe FSU becomes bowl-eligible Saturday. FSU 31, NCSU 27 Jon Marchant (season record: 7-3 ) Ah, the Fired Coaches Bowl. I was wrong about the outcome of the Pitt game, but FSU did not play very well. Normally this game would scare me, but for two reasons. It’s at home, and unlike Pitt, NC State’s defense is terrible, ranking 109th in the country per FEI, while FSU’s offense is holding steady at 19th. The other side of the ball is a more even matchup, so I think whether FSU wins or loses comes down to the Seminole offense and QB Ashton Daniels. Despite all of FSU’s injuries on offense, which have admittedly shrunk their ceiling, I think they’ll find enough explosive plays to put up enough points to become bowl-eligible. FSU 26 , NC State 16 Tim Scribble (season record: 7-3 ) If you’re reading this, you could be playing running back for Florida State this weekend; the odds may be in your favor. A limping FSU pulls off a three-game win streak. FSU 28, NC State 20 Jacob Smith (season record: 6-4) I’ve been wrong about this FSU team before, but I’m more of a believer in the “winning in all phases” cliché rather than the “momentum” cliché. NC State’s defense is pitiful, and Florida State’s offense is pretty good. Meanwhile, FSU’s defense is far below average, and NC State’s offense is bad. I think for this reason, FSU gets the win in another close game, and they FINALLY get back to a bowl game. Sad, because I’m rather fond of CJ Bailey. FSU 24, NC State 21 Curt Weiler (season record: 7-3, ATS: 3-7) If Florida State wants to get bowl eligible, I would advise it does so this week. Florida is beatable but also capable of delivering a much better result than this NC State team. Thankfully for the Seminoles, I think they get it done somewhat comfortably. The Wolfpack have been leaking some serious oil, losing their last two games and four of their last five. And it’s not to feel like the Seminoles enter this one 2-0 in the Rick Stockstill era. FSU 34, NC State 24 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 6-2) On Monday Ernie Sims said ‘we’re going to test his will’ in regard to NC State QB CJ Bailey. FSU will be down its best edge rusher Rylan Kennedy so expect a lot of heavy pressure and different looks. Bailey has been known to turn it over under consistent pressure so FSU should be able to score off some shorter fields. FSU goes bowling for the first time since 2023. FSU 34, NC State 21 Matt Minnick (season record: 7-3; ATS: 6-4) Playing in Doak for the first time under Coach Stockstill, FSU is looking to make it three in a row in ACC play for the first time since 2023. If the ‘Noles were even decently healthy I’d pick them in a runaway. NC State has given up 30+ points on 7 different occasions this season, including 41 to Duke and 34 to Syracuse in their last two games. However, FSU isn’t remotely healthy and the losses on offense have been particularly severe. Where does Stockstill turn if another running back is hurt? Can Ernie Sims’ defense step up big in back to back weeks? How will the turquoise endzones look after a few days of rain? It isn’t pretty, but the Seminoles get it done, reaching bowl eligibility with one game to go. FSU 27, NC State 23 Frank DNole (season record: 5-5) I expect FSU’s offense to score against NC State’s mid-average defense more often than not, that is, if they run Daniels to make up for the lack of running backs, even if he is banged up. That will open up the pass against NC State’s weak secondary. With news that Rylan Kennedy is now officially out, the defense’s job just got a little harder, not gonna lie. QB Bailey is predominantly a pocket passer and hasn’t been a run threat (74 attempts for 228 yards, 3.1 per carry, 22.8 yards per game, 3 TDs, long rush of 28 yards) this season. I think Ernie brings pressure more than he has. Their 6 losses have been to Virginia (5-5), Vanderbilt (4-6), Wake Forest (9-1), Stanford (5-5), Duke (7-3), and Syracuse (5-5). By Ryan Potts in College Football Published: November 25, 2026 at 11:55 am EST Florida brings a powerful ground game into Tallahassee for the Sunshine Showdown. Florida State has dropped three of its last five and leans on a turnover-prone passing attack. See my specific spread pick and price below. The No. 20 Florida Gators travel to Tallahassee to face the Florida State Seminoles on Friday, November 27. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET at Doak Campbell Stadium, and you can catch the broadcast on ABC. Florida brings a 7-4 record into this hostile environment after a gritty 34-27 win over Vanderbilt. On the other sideline, 5-6 Florida State is desperate to bounce back after a 28-10 loss to NC State. The ‘Noles need a win to secure bowl eligibility. I am looking past the emotion of the Sunshine Showdown and digging into the matchup numbers. Early Florida vs Florida State Prediction Florida wins by seven or more points. My early Florida vs Florida State prediction is a Gators win, and I expect them to win by more than a touchdown. Picking the winner and picking the cover are two different calls here, but I am backing the ranked Gators to put the final nail in the coffin for the Seminoles. Florida averages 31.6 points per game compared to 27.5 for Florida State. The Gators also allow fewer points, 26.3 per game against 26.6 for the Seminoles. The bigger edge is on the ground. Florida runs for 169.0 yards per game, and Florida State allows 171.0 rushing yards per game. That sets up Jadan Baugh perfectly. He has 980 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns, and a ground-and-pound attack lets Florida control the clock and keep the home crowd quiet. Baugh's Doak Walker Award pace has slowed considerably, but the junior still leads the SEC in rushing touchdowns and total touchdowns. With 20 rushing yards on Friday afternoon, Baugh would only be the third Gator (since 1956) with multiple 1,000-yard rushing seasons, joining Emmitt Smith and Errict Rhett. Baugh would be the only one in the group to do so in back-to-back seasons. Ball security is another focal point. Aaron Philo has thrown just five interceptions on 206 attempts, while Ashton Daniels has 14 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. It pays if the Seminoles win outright or lose by six or fewer. The win contracts are a separate question. Florida YES at 68¢ only asks whether the Gators win, so it pays even on a one-point victory. The takeaway is simple. Florida is the clear favorite to win, but the margin market is priced close to even. Sunshine Showdown Picks My Sunshine Showdown picks come down to one spread play. I am backing the road Gators to cover. Pick: Florida -6.5 (50¢ on Kalshi ) This contract pays $1 per share if Florida wins by seven or more. A Florida win by six or fewer loses, even though the Gators would win the game. Baugh against a defense allowing 171.0 rushing yards per game is the matchup I trust most. Pair that with Daniels' interceptions, and Florida should get enough possessions to pull away. Florida State has allowed four 100-yard rushers this season. Isaac Brown (Louisville) ran for a whopping 235 yards on just 17 carries. Last week, Davion Gause (NC State) tallied 134 yards. Javian Mallory (Miami, FL) and Bo MacCormack (Boston College) also cracked the century mark. Jayden Woods could help speed up that process. He leads Florida with seven sacks. Florida's defense has been spotty, but they do have four interceptions and 13 forced fumbles this season. Recent Form Heading Into the Rivalry Florida has won three of its last five. The Gators beat Texas 27-24, then lost to Georgia 27-8 and Oklahoma 23-7 before beating Kentucky 21-14 and Vanderbilt 34-27. Both of those recent wins came by exactly seven points. That is the margin this pick needs. Florida State has gone 2-3 over the same stretch. The Seminoles lost 43-35 in double overtime to Miami and 36-24 to Clemson, then beat Boston College 31-24 and Pittsburgh 16-10 before falling 28-10 to NC State. Where Florida State Can Fight Back The Seminoles are not without weapons. Daniels has thrown for 2,515 yards, and Micahi Danzy leads the team with 584 receiving yards. Ousmane Kromah adds 609 rushing yards against a Florida run defense allowing 131.9 per game. Rylan Kennedy has six sacks and could pressure Philo. If Florida State protects the football and keeps Baugh in check, this one could finish inside a touchdown. For more matchup breakdowns, visit our college football betting hub. The Florida Gators and Florida State Seminoles have historically had one of the best rivalries over the last 35 years. The 1990s were as fierce as it gets with Steve Spurrier and Bobby Bowden facing off to likely play for a national championship in multiple seasons. Then, we got Urban Meyer vs. Bobby Bowden in the 2000s before Jimbo Fisher ran the show for a decade, and the Gators had a revolving door. Now, Florida has a new head coach in Jon Sumrall, and the Seminoles finally fired Mike Norvell, with Georgia Bulldogs defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann having already accepted the job. It's a new era in the bitter rivalry, but it's primed to take a sharp step forward. Here's how our experts predicted the game. Florida 27, Florida State 17 This Seminoles team just isn't very good, and you can look at a multitude of factors to come to that conclusion. Having a head coach ready to go two weeks before early signing period is a good start, but that won't help on the field. The Gators have been playing very well defensively, and the offense, despite multiple issues, has found their way forward. There is still a lot of room to grow there, but it's going to be plenty good enough to win a rivalry game. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Florida 34, Florida State 17 The Florida-Florida State matchup is one that has certainly lost plenty of its luster over the last several years nationally, but it carried plenty of weight still in the Sunshine State. It looked like the Noles were building some momentum after firing Mike Norvell, having won two straight on the road over Boston College and Pitt, but things came crashing down on Saturday in an ugly 28-10 loss to fellow lame duck NC State. Florida is playing this one on the road, which is a good thing, given their road vs home performances with a couple of exceptions. Jaden Baugh and Aaron Philo run wild and deliver a comfortable win for the Gators. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Florida 27, Florida State 16 The Gators have been a bit of a Jekyll and Hyde team throughout the season, showing flashes of what they can be while also struggling with consistency at times. That is somewhat expected with a first-year head coach trying to establish his program while turning over a roster and building an identity. There have been some growing pains, but I think Florida puts together one of its more complete performances in this rivalry matchup. Jadan Baugh will be the difference-maker offensively, putting together a big afternoon on the ground and giving the Gators the physical presence they need to control the game. Florida State will have some success early, but I have a hard time trusting the Seminoles to put together four consistent quarters. I expect this game to be competitive through halftime before Florida starts to take control after the break. The Gators’ ability to run the football and dictate the tempo will become increasingly important as the game progresses, while Florida State struggles to find enough answers offensively. The Seminoles fade in the second half, and Florida does enough on both sides of the ball to pull away for a rivalry win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Florida 33, Florida State 20 This was once one of the best games of rivalry weekend, but in recent years, the two schools have been dealing with coaching changes and programs in flux. The Gators have outperformed many expectations in year one of the Summerall campaign, but the Seminoles finally pulled the plug on the Mike Norvell era. Even still, all bets tend to be off on rivalry weekend, and anything can happen. But not in this one. The Gators have too much firepower on offense, and the Seminoles are not an outfit that can handle the physicality and mentality that Sumrall has installed in his program. At least, not yet. Give me the Gators, comfortably. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Florida 24, Florida State 21 The Florida Gators’ season is kind of hanging on by a thread after it started out really well, but they’re still a much better team than FSU, and it’s not particularly close. Still, this game could be a close one. We saw FSU push Miami to overtime, and their offense and the way they play could do the same here. But ultimately, I see Florida winning this game. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Final Prediction for Florida vs. Florida State To nobody's surprise, our experts are in favor of the Gators here. It isn't the Seminoles year, and they are likely to fall to the orange and blue. away.blurb: The SEC availability report for Florida football's Week 12 matchup with Vanderbilt was updated on Thursday night, with no changes made for the Gators and one for the Commodores . The former still has eight players on the report — five listed as out, two who are questionable and one probable — while the latter has nine listed as out and one upgraded to available. Wide receiver Bailey Stockton and safety Bryce Thornton — the latter of whom missed the Kentucky game — are the two Gators listed as questionable. "Bailey Stockton, I'd be shocked if he doesn't play," said Sumrall. "You'd have to, like, kidnap him for him to not play, more than likely. This guy's got nine lives or 10 lives or how many were lives. You look at his own video; his was nasty. ... But we'll see as the week goes. I'd say, if you ask me who I think's most probable, it's Bailey." Cornerback Dijon Johnson is the lone Gator listed as doubtful. Vanderbilt has nine players ruled out for Saturday's game in the Swamp: cornerback Cobey Sellers, quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, edge rusher Edwin Kolenge, linebacker Josiah Broxton, running back Evan Hampton, linebacker Daniel Vollmer Jr., defensive lineman Aaron Bryant, and offensive linemen Gunner Givens and Ted Gregoire. Commodores edge defender Miles Capers was listed as probable on Wednesday's initial report , but his name has been removed, indicating that he is cleared to play on Saturday. The sixth-year player, has 25 tackles, 3.5 sacks and two forced fumbles this season. WR Bailey Stockton — questionable S Bryce Thornton — questionable Questionable (50% chance to play) Wide receiver Vernell Brown III, tight end Lacota Dippre, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji, linebacker Jaden Robinson and safety DJ Coleman are the five Gators who will not play in Saturday's SEC matchup. Brown will miss his seventh straight game with a grade-1 PCL strain he suffered against Ole Miss in Week 4 that was re-aggravated ahead of Week 9's Georgia game. The second-year receiver recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns over four appearances before being sidelined with his injury. Dippre, Ugori and Coleman all suffered ankle injuries in the win at Kentucky last week. “Dips (Dippre) is pretty substantial,” head coach Jon Sumrall said on Monday. “All those guys, you always look: is it high? Is it lateral? Is it medial? Is it a tightrope candidate? Is it not? Don’t think we have any tightrope candidates in there, from my understanding." Sumrall added, "DJ's isn't as — I'm not saying he's going to play this week. But DJ's is probably more capable of getting back fairly quick from, and then we'll see on Dip and Emeka. ... Dip's was pretty gnarly." Robinson will miss his fourth consecutive game due to an undisclosed injury. The fourth-year ILB has 26 tackles with four for loss, plus 1.5 sacks and two defended passes over seven appearances for Florida this fall. Thornton's injury was not disclosed after playing in 55 of 77 defensive snaps against Oklahoma.

home.headline: How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State
home.blurb: Florida hasn't lost to FSU since its horrific 5-7 season in 2023 when the Seminoles were a perfect 13-0 but still missed out on the College Football Playoffs. How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As of Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Florida Gators officially shut down wide receiver Vernell Brown III for the rest of the season. This is news that came as no surprise , and it's crazy to see it take as long as it did. Brown had only suited up for four games this season, but he continued to appear on injury reports leading up to Florida's 34-27 win against Vanderbilt. The 7-4 Gators certainly could've used Brown in that brutal one-win stretch from Oct. 3 to Nov. 7, but at the end of the day they bounced back terrifically from Nov. 14 onward. Brown was a crucial part of this team's 4-0 start as he recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards with a pair of touchdowns. For reference, he's still third on the team in receiving yards, proving just how valuable he was during the few games when he was around. For the Gators, it's business as usual going into the final game of the year, a rivalry showdown at Florida State. Finally, Florida's offense knows it can move on once and for all without Brown. That's not a sentence they wanted to hear back on Sept. 26, but it's been a long time coming as his status had been in doubt for the better part of two months. Brown is only a sophomore, so the Gators risking further injury by putting him back on the field was never going to be the right answer. The Florida native made an immediate impact as a freshman with his 40 receptions for 512 yards. Obviously, this season took quite a turn with those losses to Missouri and South Carolina, and it doesn't feel like a coincidence that the offense scored fewer than 20 points in those games without Brown. Running back Jadan Baugh was not a factor in either of those games either, so that also didn't help the Gators chances when they lost their offensive superstar. When Brown and Baugh were both on the field, this team looked absolutely unstoppable. Now, it'll once again be up to Aaron Philo to keep this run-game going, though he looked much better through the air against the Commodores. Florida State enters this non-conference game at 5-6 overall, fighting for bowl eligibility against a Brown-less Gators offense.

The Badgers enter the rivalry matchup coming off their most convincing win of the season, a 42-10 blowout of Purdue. Colton Joseph led the way with 187 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Darrion Dupree added another 125 yards and two scores. Minnesota has had an inconsistent season but remains a dangerous rivalry opponent . The Golden Gophers enter at 6-5 overall and 4-4 in Big Ten play, and they'll be motivated to keep the Axe after defeating Wisconsin 17-7 last season. The biggest factor will be whether Wisconsin can carry its offensive momentum into the rivalry game. Minnesota's defense presents a tougher challenge than Purdue, but the Badgers have shown what their offense can look like when Joseph and the rushing attack are clicking. Playing at Camp Randall should give Wisconsin another advantage. One would expect a competitive rivalry game, but the Badgers seem have enough momentum to finish the regular season with a statement win. Fussell's potential return would be especially important for the Wildcats. The defensive back has been sidelined since the Indiana game on Sept. 25 and has been a significant absence in Northwestern's secondary. He is one of the team's key defensive players, and getting him back on the field would provide a major boost to a defense that has dealt with several injuries throughout the season. Fussell has been missed over the past several weeks, particularly with Northwestern facing some of the more explosive offenses in the Big Ten. His potential return would give the Wildcats another experienced option in the secondary and could help improve their coverage and overall defensive communication. Adeyi is another important name to watch. He went down with an injury during Northwestern's loss to Ohio State . Seeing him listed as questionable rather than out is an encouraging development, although his availability will ultimately depend on how he progresses before Saturday. Having both players potentially available would be a significant development for a Northwestern defense that needs all the help it can get. The Wildcats have shown an ability to create turnovers and make important plays defensively, but they have also struggled to contain explosive plays and prevent opponents from putting together big drives. Fussell and Adeyi potentially returning would be a positive step in the right direction. 122nd time since 1897, Michigan and Ohio State will meet in a rivalry known as "The Game." Photo By - Reuters Connect. Charles Woodson (2) and Archie Griffin (45) are two key figures in the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry. Arguably the greatest rivalry in all of sports returns in Week 13 of the college football season, with Ohio State hosting Michigan at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio, at noon ET (FOX) on Saturday, Nov. 28. This year's edition of the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry , known simply as The Game, is different from recent years, with both programs enduring down seasons and neither contending for a national championship. Some would argue that makes this the purest version of the rivalry, with both teams fueled by their dislike for each other and little else. Ohio State is a 10.5-point favorite, and my college football picks back the Buckeyes to win big. Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry history: The Game Wins (official; six ties) 9 (1901-1909) Longest win streak 8 (2012-2019) Largest margin of victory 1027-367-36 (.731) Program record 997-342-53 (.735) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks Few rivalries feature two teams as successful as Michigan and Ohio State . That history makes their mutual hatred even more intense. The Wolverines and the Buckeyes have both won plenty of national championships, produced multiple Heisman Trophy winners, and sent countless players to the NFL, but more than anything else, they take pride in beating each other. This rivalry is built as much on program success as it is on animosity. Michigan has more wins than any other program in college football history, and Ohio State has a higher winning percentage than any other program in college football history. The Game often has major implications for the national championship and the Heisman Trophy race. It all began in 1897, and The Game has been played every season since 1918, except in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Its history stretches from Fielding Yost's early dominance through Woody Hayes and Bo Schembechler's Ten-Year War, Jim Tressel and Urban Meyer's successful runs, and Jim Harbaugh's revival of Michigan. This is the college football rivalry. Recent Michigan-Ohio State results Nov. 29, 2025 27-9 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-9.5) Nov. 30, 2024 13-10 (Michigan) Michigan (+19.5) Nov. 25, 2023 30-24 (Michigan) Michigan (-3.5) Nov. 26, 2022 45-23 (Michigan) Michigan (+8.5) Nov. 27, 2021 42-27 (Michigan) Michigan (+7) Nov. 30, 2019 56-27 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-9) Nov. 24, 2018 62-39 (Ohio State) Ohio State (+3.5) Nov. 25, 2017 31-20 (Ohio State) Michigan (+12.5) Nov. 26, 2016 30-27 (Ohio State) Michigan (+4.5) Nov. 28, 2015 42-13 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-1.5) History of the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry When did the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry start? The Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry began in 1897 and was immediately a natural rivalry because of the bordering states' history with the Toledo War (a boundary dispute between the states over the Toledo Strip). The Wolverines won the first matchup on Oct. 16, 1897, in Ann Arbor, 34-0. The programs didn't meet again until a 0-0 tie in 1900, then played every season through 1912. Michigan went 12-0-2 against Ohio State from 1897 to 1912. The Buckeyes didn't win The Game for the first time until 1919, beating Michigan 13-3 to spark a three-game winning streak. However, Michigan owned the rivalry, for the most part, until Hayes arrived in 1951. The Wolverines went 32-12-4 against Ohio State from 1897 to 1950. Why is it called The Game? Michigan vs. Ohio State is known to most as The Game because of its importance to both fan bases and college football nationally. The matchup has closed out the regular season since 1935, and usually there's plenty on the line when these teams meet. Before Big Ten expansion, the winner of The Game would frequently win the conference and head to the Rose Bowl for a chance at a national title. And in later years, The Game would play a key role in setting the Big Ten Championship Game matchup. The loser of The Game generally considers the season a disappointment. What was the Ten-Year War? What kicked off the Ten-Year War between Michigan and Ohio State was the Wolverines hiring Hayes' protege, Schembechler, in 1969. Schembechler had been an assistant under Hayes at Ohio State from 1958 to 1962 before following in Hayes' footsteps and becoming head coach at Miami (OH). Both Hayes (1949-1950) and Schembechler (1963-1968) coached at Miami (Ohio) before taking over Ohio State and Michigan. Hayes went 12-6 against Michigan in The Game from 1951-1968 and flipped the once maize and blue-dominated rivalry to the scarlet and grey. That led Michigan in a new direction with the hiring of Schembechler, who immediately made his presence felt. In Schembechler's first game against Ohio State, Michigan pulled off "the upset of the century" by beating the No. 1 Buckeyes 24-12 and ending their 22-game winning streak. That victory marked the beginning of the Ten-Year War. From 1970 to 1975, in four of the six meetings, both Ohio State and Michigan were ranked in the top five. During the Ten-Year War, the programs shared the Big Ten title multiple times, with Michigan ultimately having the upper hand, going 5-4-1 against Ohio State. The war ended after the 1978 season, when Hayes was fired for punching Clemson linebacker Charlie Bauman after an interception in the Gator Bowl. It was during the Ten-Year War that Ohio State began its tradition of referring to Michigan as "That Team Up North" when Hayes referred to the Wolverines as such. Best moments in the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry The Snow Bowl (1950) Among the most famous games in the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry, the Snow Bowl was exactly what it sounds like: a game in a blizzard. The blizzard was so bad that the Buckeyes were given the option to cancel the game (they would have won the Big Ten title by default if they had), but Ohio State wanted to play its rival. All in all, the teams combined to punt the ball 45 times, with many of the punts coming on first down as they battled for field position and hoped the other team would fumble. Michigan would block two punts, one resulting in a safety and the other a touchdown, to win 9-3. The Wolverines didn't complete a single pass or gain a single first down, but took home the Big Ten title with the win. Ohio State head coach Wes Fesler would resign after the loss, leading to Hayes being hired. The Upset of the Century (1969) In Schembechler's first game against his former boss, Michigan would upset undefeated No. 1-ranked Ohio State 24-12. The Buckeyes were riding a 22-game winning streak and gunning for their second straight national title, but an all-time performance from Barry Pierson (three interceptions and a 60-yard punt return that set up a touchdown) would end Ohio State's shot at a championship. Tech couple Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer is concerned about the Buckeyes heading into their game against Michigan Getty Michael Gallagher · HEAVY Mon, November 23, 2026 at 8:25 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 29: Bryce Underwood #19 of the Michigan Wolverines is pursued by Kenyatta Jackson Jr. #97 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the fourth quarter at Michigan Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty Ohio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey after losing his last two games Getty It's been a rough month for the Ohio State Buckeyes. Ohio State started 6-1 but has lost three of its last four games. The latest was Saturday's 31-28 loss at Nebraska, which officially knocked the Buckeyes out of the College Football Playoff race. All that's left now is "The Game" against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday in Columbus. On paper, Ohio State has the better roster. Even former Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer admits that. Meyer, who went 7-0 against Michigan during his time in Columbus, still picked Ohio State to win. However, it sounds like he wouldn't be all that surprised if Michigan ended up leaving Columbus with a win. Urban Meyer's 1 Major Michigan Concern GettyMichigan and Ohio State both head into the Big Game with serious question marks Meyer spoke on stage at an event in a video posted Sunday by 10TV Sports' Adam King, and he didn't sugarcoat where Ohio State stands. "The roster's better — Ohio State — but the best unit performing right now is the Wolverine defense. And that concerns me a little bit," Meyer said . "They really hammered UCLA. You got to think, the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible — they're last in the country. And so, to still have decent numbers — only one team has over 21 points on them all year, and that was Oregon — that's a legit defense. "On offense, we got the best player in the country, maybe the best player to ever play college football — that's how good Jeremiah is. But we also have a backup quarterback, and the offensive line is not playing great. So, I think this is going to be a rock fight; a low-scoring game, and I think whoever punches the hardest is going to win the game. I expect it to be a 17-10, 17-14 game and I got the Buckeyes." The numbers back up Meyer's remarks. Michigan ranks 17th nationally in scoring defense (17.5 points per game) and ninth in total defense (278.3 yards per game). And Oregon, which beat Michigan 31-7, is the only team to score more than 21 points on the Wolverines all season. The Wolverines' defense was at its best last Saturday in an 18-16 triple-overtime upset of previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA. Michigan held the Bruins to 187 yards through three quarters and finished with three forced turnovers and four sacks. Why Urban Meyer Expects a Rock Fight vs. Michigan GettyOhio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey The biggest reason for Meyer's worry is at quarterback. Starter Julian Sayin hurt his right (throwing) arm in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17, and he isn't expected back for Michigan. That leaves true freshman Luke Fahey under center. Fahey went 16 of 27 for 259 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception at Nebraska. But nearly all of that came early: He was 9 of 12 for 163 yards and two scores in the first half, then 7 of 15 for 96 yards after halftime. Jeremiah Smith did his part (six catches, 165 yards, two touchdowns), tying Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record with 17 receiving TDs. Meyer also didn't pull any punches when it came to the other side of the ball for Michigan. "That defense is legit, legit because that offense is pathetic up there. It's the worst offense in college football, yet they're in almost all the games," Meyer said . "Their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal. Our defense has been up-and-down a little bit, but their offense stinks. I see this being a very low-scoring game. This is Ohio State-Wolverine football. The toughest team is going to win this game." Michigan's offense isn't quite the worst in the country, but it's close. The Wolverines rank 131st nationally in scoring (18.3 points per game). It's quite a shift for Meyer, who reportedly called the 2026 Wolverines a "train wreck" in early October. The Buckeyes (7-4) and Wolverines (6-5) kick off at noon ET Saturday at Ohio Stadium on Fox. Tech couple Michigan vs Ohio State Prediction: Who Will Save Its Season? Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Debate it all you want, but Michigan vs Ohio State, in football, is the best rivalry in all of American sports. Alabama vs Auburn is as nasty as it gets, but that's a high-end, in-state war. Yankees vs Red Sox and Bears vs Packers – those get played several times a year. Duke vs North Carolina in basketball gets played at least twice. With Michigan and Ohio State, you have two behemoth universities from two different states, and it all comes down to this one game that, when it's at its biggest and best, stops the sports world cold. This isn't at its biggest and best this year, which means it's all about the rivalry. Trust me, you can be Michigan or Ohio State and win the national title, but if you don't beat the other, the season has a hole in it. As bad as the season has been for the Wolverines or Buckeyes, someone's year will be made. Sep 12, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; Michigan Wolverines head coahc Kyle Whittingham looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Michigan vs Ohio State: Quick Hits Ohio State actually has a very, very distant shot at getting into the Big Ten Championship. 1) The Buckeyes have to win, 2) Indiana, Iowa, Oregon, and USC have to lose, and 3) Maryland, Rutgers, and Wisconsin have to win. Michigan finally got bowl-eligible with its thrilling win over UCLA last week. Ohio State won 27-9 last year to break a run of four straight Michigan wins. The Buckeyes haven't beaten the Wolverines in Columbus since 2018. How To Watch Michigan vs Ohio State Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Ohio Stadium, Columbus, OH – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why Michigan Will Win The defense continues to be a force. It's ninth in the nation overall, with a nasty run defense that held up well against both UCLA's pounding style last week and Oregon's flash and speed before that. Rutgers is the only team to average more than four yards per carry against this Wolverine bunch. Ohio State's running game isn't good enough to carry the team. This is about as simple as it gets for a Wolverine team without a steady passing game. Run the ball well, force field goals, repeat. The Michigan ground attack hasn't been too bad, and in this, it just has to keep the clock moving – having Bryce Underwood under center should help. Ohio State is 1-4 when allowing over 85 rushing yards. Michigan is 6-2 when running for more than 80. But … Why Ohio State Will Win The Michigan passing attack is just plain putrid. It actually worked against Iowa, of all teams, but it's wildly inconsistent and doesn't do a thing downfield. Ohio State has to get up fast. It was able to do it in the 41-28 loss to Oregon, and scored first last week against Nebraska. Positive momentum will be everything to this Buckeye bunch. It won't have a problem if Michigan tries to keep running, but it does have to keep Underwood from finding a passing groove. The Buckeyes are now 0-4 against teams that connect on more than 60% of their passes. Underwood is hitting just 55% of his throws on the year. Michigan vs Ohio State Prediction, Betting Lines Will Jeremiah Smith do enough to take home the Heisman? This is his one final chance to make his case, and Michigan will have him wrapped up tight. The star caught three passes for 40 yards and a key score in last year's Buckeye win, and made five grabs for 35 yards and a touchdown in 2024. Ohio State quarterback Luke Fahey will have another nice game – he hasn't been the problem in this rough run over the last month. He'll hit one deep shot to Smith, and that will be about enough. This year's edition of the game won't be up there in terms of implications , but neither team wants to lose to the other. Both teams are eliminated from winning the Big Ten and making the College Football Playoff, which will be the first season that neither team is in the playoff since 2018. It's been a parity-filled season of football and both the Wolverines and Buckeyes are on the wrong side of things. Michigan is coming off a massive home win against previously unbeaten UCLA. The Wolverines took the Bruins into triple overtime and Bryce Underwood found Jalen Hoffman in the corner of the end zone to win the game. Ohio State, however, faltered once again and has now lost three of its last four games. This time, to Nebraska on the road. Michigan's odds of beating Ohio State USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect In the last four games, Michigan has gone 2-2 with losses to both Michigan State and Oregon. While the Buckeyes are 1-3 with losses against USC, Oregon, and Nebraska. Neither team is playing well, but boh teams are playing poorly in different areas. Even so, ESPN's FPI isn't giving Michigan much of a chance to go on the road and win the game. The Wolverines have just a 10.8% chance to beating the Buckeyes this weekend, per the advanced analytics. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , Ohio State opened as a 14-point favorite, but the Buckeyes are now a 10-point favorite to beat Michigan. Which means some money has gone on the Wolverines recently. Two teams with two different faults Saturday will be a battle between good on good and bad on bad. Michigan's offense remains difficult to watch, although running back Savion Hiter has been a glimmer of hope in the last two weeks, rushing for over 100 yards. Ohio State's defense has really come apart and has allowed 30, 41, 31 points, respectively, in its last three losses. So we will see which unit can be slightly better on Saturday. And it's a different story on the other side of the ball. The Buckeyes might be playing backup quarterback Luke Fahey, but Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith, who can win in triple coverage. Michigan will have its hands full defending him on Saturday, but clearly, the Wolverines' strength is their defense. Can Michigan's defense win the game this weekend? If the Wolverines do win, it will be because Jay Hill and Co. get the job done. away.headline: Blake Frazer, Rod Moore, Andrew Marsh Headline Michigan's Initial Injury Report vs. UCLA
away.blurb: We knew that JJ Buchanan was going to be out. Kyle Whittingham said so on Monday, but it's very concerning to see the likes of Andrew Marsh, and even Channing Goodwin to a certain extent on the list. Without Buchanan, Marsh is the certified alpha on the team and will be a key part of the Wolverines' passing attack — especially if there is any hope to get it going. And the offensive line remains a major issue. Blake Frazier is now officially out and the Wolverines played without him last weekend. Brady Norton is questionable, too, and the Wolverines could opt to play both Manuel Beigel and Marky Walbridge once again this weekend. After back-to-back losses to Michigan State and Oregon, the Wolverines are looking to get back in the win column. In fact, Michigan needs one more win in the last two weeks in order to go bowling. The Wolverines haven't missed a bowl game since 2014, the final year of Brady Hoke in Ann Arbor. If Michigan is going to gain bowl eligibility this weekend, the Wolverines are going to have to earn it. Michigan will host UCLA, which hasn't lost a game all year. The Bruins are one of the most surprising teams in college football. Despite losing Nico Iamaleava for the season, Bob Chesney has turned to his backup quarterback, but it's only resulted in success. If the Wolverines are going to beat UCLA , it's going to have to get the job done without a few players. Here's how Michigan's initial availability report looks heading into the Wolverines' Week 12 game against UCLA. More concern regarding the offense Michigan will also rely on Travis Johnson and Salesi Moa moving forward. Whittingham noted that tight end Mason Bonner could also see some play. It's also concerning to see Rod Moore on the list after he played last weekend against Oregon. The Wolverines' secondary got beat a few times against Oregon, and having a veteran back there like Moore would only help against UCLA. away.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood dealing with injury heading into Ohio State game
away.blurb: At his press conference on Monday morning, Michigan head football coach Kyle Whittingham said that sophomore Bryce Underwood is set to start in The Game this weekend against Ohio State. However, we’ll see if he’s able to even play at all. Per 247Sports’ Matt Zenitz, Underwood is dealing with a lower-body injury that he suffered during Saturday’s stunning upset win over UCLA. His status is “in question” heading into The Game in Columbus this weekend. Underwood has had quite the roller coaster season. He started the first six games of the season before freshman Tommy Carr took over after halftime of the Penn State game. Carr was then benched two weeks ago during the game at Oregon, and Underwood has taken every snap since. Despite the injury, Whittingham told the media on Monday morning that Underwood is “the guy” at quarterback, and that “barring anything unforeseen, getting dinged up in practice or something like that,” he will start against the Buckeyes on Saturday. Underwood completed just 11-of-24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown on Saturday vs UCLA. He also ran 13 times for five yards, losing one fumble in the process. On the season, he has completed 85-of-156 passes (54.5 percent) for 1,077 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions, while also running 76 times for 230 yards and an additional two scores. Should Underwood not be able to play in this one, Carr will be the next man up for the Wolverines. The true freshman has completed 67-of-106 passes this season for 686 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s also ran 49 times for 138 yards and three touchdowns. Michigan vs Ohio State is set for a noon kickoff on FOX.

Wolverines Football Updated: Nov. 24, 2026, 9:28 a.m. | Published: Nov. 23, 2026, 11:55 a.m. Aaron McMann | amcmann@mlive.com ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Kyle Whittingham said Monday morning that Michigan football would be sticking with Bryce Underwood at quarterback this week. Given what happened over the weekend, the Wolverines’ upset win over No. 4 UCLA, 18-16, in overtime, it makes sense. The sophomore didn’t put up impressive numbers, but did enough to help the team -- and completed the game-winning two-point conversion throw. “Bryce is the guy,” Whittingham told reporters ahead of Saturday’s rivalry showdown at Ohio State (12 p.m., FOX). “Bryce is the guy and Tommy (Carr) is the No. 2.” Whittingham did add a stipulator, calling it the plan “barring any(thing) unforeseen” like “getting dinged up in practice or something like that. “That’s how it will be,” Whittingham continued. Roughly 45 minutes later, CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reported that Underwood suffered a lower-body injury in the win over UCLA that left his status in question for Saturday’s game. Soon after, national reporters from On3 and ESPN confirmed the injury to Underwood. The quarterback appeared fine physically as he spoke to the press after the game on Saturday, calling it “a blessing” to get a second chance at being the Wolverines’ starting quarterback. Michigan will be required to submit a player availability report to the Big Ten beginning on Wednesday, with updates expected daily leading up to Saturday’s game in Columbus. away.headline: Kyle Whittingham updates Michigan injuries ahead of Ohio State game
away.blurb: While Marky Walbridge has improved week-over-week serving as the Wolverines' right tackle, Blake Frazier -- though better at left tackle -- would give Michigan that much better of an opportunity. While JJ Buchanan and Andrew Sprague are ruled out, getting Frazier back would be a big boost in the arm. There are two other players who very well could return -- another offensive lineman in Brady Norton, as well as running back Jordan Marshall, who has missed the past few games. Though the Wolverines have solid replacements at each of their positions, Whittingham would love to have both available. And at least one will be. “Brady Norton, we hope to get back this week,” Whittingham said. “He would have been available last week or on Saturday in an emergency situation. JJ, out for the year, like we said. Jordan Marshall. He hopefully will be back. It’s going to be close, but we’re hoping that we get him back this week.” “Jake Guarnera is a tough kid,” Whittingham said. “He has played through a lot of pain. Again, we’re not going to put a guy out there. Our trainers, our medical staff isn’t going to put anybody out there that is going to be in danger of furthering an injury. But he has been able to endure a lot of discomfort, and a lot of guys would not have been able to play with the discomfort that he’s been able to play with. So, credit to Jake. He’s a warrior.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. -- Michigan football has been shorthanded all year, and it'll hope to be closer to full strength on Saturday when it heads to Columbus to take on the most gettable version of Ohio State in more than a decade. The Wolverines and Buckeyes have four or more losses each entering The Game for the first time since 1966, and while there are questions about Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood, who was revealed as having an injury on Monday, there are certainly others the maize and blue would love to have back. Kyle Whittingham isn't sure whether he'll be able to go or not, but he does believe he's progressing. “He’s making progress, I can tell you that,” Whittingham said. “But we still do not have a definitive thumbs up or thumbs down for this week.” One player not spoken of as much is center Jake Guarnera, who has played through injury all year. He hasn't been so bad that he could make things worse, but he's battled through everything that's been thrown at him. Michigan and Ohio State are set to kick off at 12:10 p.m. EST at Ohio Stadium, with The Game set to air on Fox. The Wolverines and Buckeyes have four or more losses each entering The Game for the first time since 1966, and while there are questions about Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood, who was revealed as having an injury on Monday, there are certainly others the maize and blue would love to have back. Kyle Whittingham isn't sure whether he'll be able to go or not, but he does believe he's progressing. “He’s making progress, I can tell you that,” Whittingham said. “But we still do not have a definitive thumbs up or thumbs down for this week.” One player not spoken of as much is center Jake Guarnera, who has played through injury all year. He hasn't been so bad that he could make things worse, but he's battled through everything that's been thrown at him. Michigan and Ohio State are set to kick off at 12:10 p.m. EST at Ohio Stadium, with The Game set to air on Fox. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. How to watch Louisville Cardinals vs. Kentucky Wildcats Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 12:00 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a +2.5-point underdog after the Wildcats were previously -1.5-point favorites. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 35.6% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction: Before the season started, I predicted Kentucky would win six games but lose to Louisville, believing Will Stein would have too much emotion coaching against his former team, where he once played. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Although this year’s game will be played at Kroger Field, I believe the Wildcats will pull off another victory in a high-scoring contest. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. Tech couple Clemson Given Lackluster Prediction Ahead of South Carolina Showdown (Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports - Clemson Tue, November 24, 2026 at 11:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Clemson Tigers were able to take down the Duke Blue Devils on the road last week, picking up a massive win for the season. Clemson is now 7-4 on the season, with the team having won four of its last six games overall. The Tigers have rebounded nicely from a poor opening part of the season, despite a lackluster offense all year. But as the Tigers prepare for the final week of the regular season, the only focus is on getting a win over the rival South Carolina Gamecocks. Clemson will be hosting South Carolina in the game, giving themselves a slight edge entering the contest. South Carolina will come into the game with a record of 6-5 for the season, coming off two straight blow out losses. The Gamecocks have lost by a score of 34-6 in two straight weeks, and they will try to bounce back this week against Clemson. Both sides understand the rivalry aspect of this game, with the Tigers wanting to add another win to the season's resume. But South Carolina won't go down quietly, looking to spoil the Tigers' final home game of the year. Heading into the game, the Tigers are being viewed as the underdogs, despite having the better record than South Carolina. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson has a 44.2 percent chance of taking down the Gamecocks this week at home. Quarterback Trent Pearman will likely get the starting nod in this game after leading the Tigers to a win last week. Pearman did well enough for Clemson to win, and it seems that the program wants to see more from him in this game. Overall, Pearman went 17-of-27 for 164 yards, with no touchdown passes against the Blue Devils. But he did rush for 51 yards and a touchdown, showing that he can be a dual-threat option for Clemson. If Pearman can continue to help the offense, it could give Clemson an opportunity to grab the win. Clemson's defense has been strong all year, and South Carolina's offense has been very stagnant over the last few weeks. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney has been criticized all season long , but if this team could get a win over the Gamecocks, it could go a long way for him. The 2026 season won't be seen as a complete success, but after how it started, the Tigers may end the year on a high note.

picks.headline: Former Clemson football safety Khalil Barnes picks off South Carolina
picks.blurb: Former Clemson football safety Khalil Barnes picks off South Carolina - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Steelers release Aaron Rodgers Latest CFP rankings MLB free agency updates NBA Cup roundup Viral Ga. Tech couple Former Clemson football safety Khalil Barnes picks off South Carolina Drew Landon, Clemson Wire · Clemson Wire Sun, November 22, 2026 at 3:24 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Khalil Barnes may have traded orange for red and black, but habits from longtime friends are hard to get rid of. The former Clemson football player came down with a late third-quarter interception against rivals South Carolina on Saturday night, ending a Gamecocks red-zone threat and helping top-ranked Georgia hold a 27-6 lead going into the fourth quarter. South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was driving inside the Georgia 22 when he forced a throw into traffic. Barnes was lingering and waiting. The pick took away South Carolina's best chance to cut into the deficit and handed the ball straight back to the Bulldogs. It was the only turnover of the night for either team at that point and the only one South Carolina couldn't afford at the time. The Gamecocks, ranked 21st at 6-4, had managed just two field goals before the interception. Georgia, 9-1 and ranked first, had already built a two-score cushion behind two Nate Frazier rushing touchdowns and a pair of field goals from Peyton Woodring. For Clemson fans, the sight of Barnes snuffing out a South Carolina drive had to feel familiar probably even a tad bit confusing for the head to digest. He left Death Valley, but nobody let his instincts know that they should do the same. Somewhere in Upstate South Carolina, Tigers fans are watching a former player in a Bulldogs jersey do exactly what they would have asked of him, and deciding whether to be proud or just slightly annoyed that it's happening in another uniform. Barnes may be wearing a Georgia G now, but the Tiger paw is clearly still stamped somewhere in his blood. The Gamecocks will need to regroup quickly if they are to win this one. Georgia leads 27-6 with the fourth quarter just starting up. This was written in the fourth quarter of the Georgia vs. South Carolina game.
