away.blurb: Teams have released their first injury reports for the week. The most glaring omission from the report is the name of LaNorris Sellers . After being listed as questionable last week, Sellers was unable to participate against the Arkansas Razorbacks, which led to a blowout 34-6 loss. Sellers’s presence is a non-negotiable if the Gamecocks want to pull off an upset against the number one ranked Georgia Bulldogs , who arguably have the best defensive unit in the country. The Bulldogs have limited some of the best quarterbacks and offenses in the conference to a standstill, but Sellers could be one of the toughest tests they face all season. Though Sellers will be back, injury issues still loom over the Gamecocks. Leading rusher Matt Fuller IV is out. Receivers Mazeo Bennett Jr. and Nyck Harbor are listed as questionable along with EDGE’s Dylan Stewart and Anthony Addison. DB Judge Collier is also listed as questionable. away.headline: South Carolina vs. Georgia: Kickoff time, TV channel, injury report, odds
away.blurb: WR Nitro Tuggle, DB Jalewis Soloman, WR Jayden Sellers, RB Matt Fuller, EDGE Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josiah Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. WR Mazeo Bennett, EDGE Dylan Stewart, DB Judge Collier, WR Nyck Harbor and EDGE Anthony Addison are all listed as questionable. All five of those players are starters at their respective positions and would be a massive loss should they not play this weekend. What’s going on at QB? There was confusion galore around South Carolina’s quarterback room last week. Is LaNorris Sellers healthy? Would he be available? Is he going to play? What’s the definition of probable? Does anything anyone says really mean anything? The answer to those questions was that Cutter Woods started at quarterback for South Carolina in its loss to Arkansas. USC offensive coordinator Kendal Briles said “all” of the Gamecock quarterbacks practiced on Wednesday. It remains to be seen if Sellers will return from the ankle injury he sustained vs. Texas A&M or if Woods will get the second start of his career. Is all CFP hope lost? South Carolina’s hopes of making the College Football Playoff seemed completely lost after it was upset on the road by Arkansas last week. After all, there’s no way a team with four losses who was just defeated by an unranked team would stick around in the CFP rankings…right? Wrong. South Carolina remained in the CFP Top 25 , only dropping from No. 17 to No. 21. The odds of making the playoff are very slim but should South Carolina find a way to win out by beating No. 1 Georgia and Clemson then there’s a world where its playoff odds may graduate to just slim . Shane Beamer and the No. 21 Gamecocks will face No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. The game will kick off at 7:30 p.m. and be televised nationally on ABC. South Carolina (6-4, 4-4 SEC) is coming off a loss to Arkansas last week. Meanwhile, Georgia (9-1, 7-1 SEC) is coming off a win over Missouri at home. Georgia leads the all-time series over South Carolina 55-19-2. The Bulldogs have won the last four games in the series, including the last matchup in 2023. South Carolina’s last win in the series came in upset fashion in 2019. The Gamecocks haven’t beat Georgia at home in Columbia since 2014. Here’s everything you need to know about Saturday’s game. This is the seventh time the show, which airs from 9 a.m. to noon, has come to Columbia.

Rivalry weekend is upon us, a chance to right wrongs and establish year-long bragging rights in the face of a hated opponent. TCU has won five of the last six in the series, but that was prior to Texas Tech's rise in the NIL era, with a roster vastly superior to most Big 12 opponents. Tommy Castellanos had his first multi-turnover game with the Red Raiders last week, so look for him to be more protective of the football en route to the program's second straight Big 12 title game appearance. ... Texas Tech 31, TCU 14. No. 25 Nebraska at No. 13 Iowa (-4.5) Hummer ( Nebraska +4.5) : These are pretty similar teams. The difference is Iowa is a bit better up front, and Nebraska's QB, Anthony Colandrea , comes with a slightly higher ceiling. I like the way Nebraska is playing of late, and I think the against-the-spread value is with the Huskers. But I also believe Iowa is the better team and far more likely to execute down the stretch in a close game. Iowa eeks by to reach 10-2. … Iowa 20, Nebraska 17. But … all the advanced data says that this will be a very close game. Like within a point or two. I just don't see that. Crawford (Florida -5.5) : Did the Seminoles get caught looking ahead to rivalry weekend last week? I was stunned to flip the channel and see NC State with a double-digit lead in the second half at Doak Campbell. That was an embarrassing loss, one that might keep this team out of the postseason unless they find a way to beat the Gators. I don't see it happening if Florida finds some semblance of consistency defensively and gets a few stops early in the matchup. ... Florida 26, Florida State 17. No. 3 Texas (-10.5) at Texas A&M Hummer (Texas -10.5) : Have you seen the Texas A&M offense recently? The Aggies haven't hit double digits in a game since October, and it's not going to get any easier against a top-10 Texas defense. It's a rivalry game. The Aggies will play hard. His uber-talented defense against a quarterback making his second start? Kentucky's frail with three straight losses, but this one feels different for Will Stein in his first rival setting with the Wildcats. After playing three straight challenging SEC defenses, Kenny Minchey gets a break against an opponent that ranks 10th in the ACC in total yards allowed. ... Kentucky 28, Louisville 27. But there's plenty of pressure on both coaches. Kyle Whittingham remains very much on the hot seat. Ryan Day is amid the worst season of his Ohio State coaching career. I think the Buckeyes win. Odds may be shifting the Trojans' way but these three factors can guarantee a upset victory. 1. Defense Flusters UCLA Quarterback Madden Iamaleava Nov 21, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; UCLA quarterback Madden Iamaleava (10) gets ready to take a snap the Michigan Wolverines in the second half at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Bruins might have Ty Dieffenbach listed as "probable," but it could be more of a guise to avoid the outcome Florida State had in 2023. For now, Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Nico Iamaleava, is expected to start, and the Trojans' defense should be licking its chops. When the sophomore entered the game, he looked hesitant and unprepared. The result was a rough outing, failing to make a complete pass and rushing for negative yards. On top of his depth chart status at the start of the year, Iamaleava has little high school experience to lean on as well. Madden backed up Nico at Warren High (Downey, Calif.) from his freshman to sophomore year. He made a total of 17 appearances during that time, but it was a small sample size. Then in 2023, Madden became the full-time starter. In 13 games, he threw for 3,626 yards, 43 touchdowns and only four interceptions, per MaxPreps. He showed flashes of being a dynamic runner as well, rushing for 305 yards and three scores. A fallout at Warren led to a midseason transfer attempt to Long Beach Poly. Ultimately, Iamaleava did not play his senior year. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney reacts to a play against Michigan during the third overtime at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Plus, the Bruins' offense has already been struggling under Dieffenbach - four interceptions in seven games, two of which came from Dieffenbach against Michigan in Week 12, No. 98 in points per trip inside the opponent's 40-yard line and a lack of explosive plays despite having an excellent rushing attack. As great as coach Bob Chesney has been this season, it seems like a tall task to have the young Iamaleava ready on Nov. 28. Despite a slow start, USC's defense came to play against a red-hot Maryland offense. Despite having a low pressure rate of 28 percent, the line was able to record four quarterback hits. The defensive front also disrupted the Terrapins' run game with four tackles for loss (seven yards). More importantly, the secondary came away with three interceptions. With a lack of an outside threat, USC can focus on bringing the pressure from the interior and a blitzing nickelback. Desman Stephens II and Deven Bryant have done an excellent job leading the middle of the defense, and they will be huge in slowing down the Bruins' lead back, Wayne Knight. away.blurb: Ending the season on a two-game losing skid and having the quarterback injury will allow the committee to leave them out, potentially for another SEC team or to take three Big 12 teams. Once Dieffenbach was removed from the game, many felt like that was the end of UCLA’s season. While his status is uncertain for this week against USC, Dieffenbach is dealing with a minor hip injury. Dieffenbach is expected to be available for the College Football Playoff should UCLA clinch a bid,” Thamel wrote . How legit this report is unclear. There is some thought that UCLA could say Dieffenbach is questionable so as not to get punished by the committee for a quarterback injury, as Florida State was years ago when Jordan Travis was injured, and FSU, despite going undefeated, was left out of the playoffs. The UCLA Bruins had their undefeated season end on the road in overtime against the Michigan Wolverines. UCLA was a major surprise this season, entering their road game against Michigan at 10-0. However, the Bruins were knocked for their schedule, as UCLA hadn’t had many big wins outside of Oregon, right after Dante Moore was lost for the season, and the Ducks were struggling on offense. Although UCLA was undefeated, they still weren’t getting much respect because of their schedule, as the College Football Playoff Committee had them ranked behind a two-loss Alabama team. Now, after the Bruins suffered an overtime loss to Michigan, UCLA will likely drop a ton in the rankings, as there are question marks around them. The Bruins already lost starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava to injury, and against Michigan, backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach also got injured. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see the committee use the quarterback injuries against UCLA and drop them further in the rankings than they should be. home.headline: UCLA Bruins face do-or-die game against USC amid injury update
home.blurb: Ending the season on a two-game losing skid and having the quarterback injury will allow the committee to leave them out, potentially for another SEC team or to take three Big 12 teams. Once Dieffenbach was removed from the game, many felt like that was the end of UCLA’s season. However, ESPN college football insider Pete Thamel revealed the injury isn’t considered long-term and there is a chance he will be available in the playoffs. “Sources: UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach isn’t expected to be out long-term. While his status is uncertain for this week against USC, Dieffenbach is dealing with a minor hip injury. Dieffenbach is expected to be available for the College Football Playoff should UCLA clinch a bid,” Thamel wrote . How legit this report is unclear. There is some thought that UCLA could say Dieffenbach is questionable so as not to get punished by the committee for a quarterback injury, as Florida State was years ago when Jordan Travis was injured, and FSU, despite going undefeated, was left out of the playoffs. The UCLA Bruins had their undefeated season end on the road in overtime against the Michigan Wolverines. UCLA was a major surprise this season, entering their road game against Michigan at 10-0. However, the Bruins were knocked for their schedule, as UCLA hadn’t had many big wins outside of Oregon, right after Dante Moore was lost for the season, and the Ducks were struggling on offense. Although UCLA was undefeated, they still weren’t getting much respect because of their schedule, as the College Football Playoff Committee had them ranked behind a two-loss Alabama team. Now, after the Bruins suffered an overtime loss to Michigan, UCLA will likely drop a ton in the rankings, as there are question marks around them. The Bruins already lost starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava to injury, and against Michigan, backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach also got injured. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see the committee use the quarterback injuries against UCLA and drop them further in the rankings than they should be. Tech couple Corbie Craig Contributing writer Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College football rivalry week is here, and some of the toughest teams to price are the ones making changes this late in the season. Oklahoma has won three straight with Jason Witten calling plays, Minnesota just won after changing its offensive coordinator, and Wisconsin got a big performance from a quarterback who had lost his starting job. There are reasons to believe those offenses are improving, but I want to be careful about how much of last Saturday carries into this week. I'm starting with three unders, looking at the way these teams have been moving the ball and how much work it takes them to score. Here are my three early Week 13 bets. No. 19 Oklahoma at No. 24 Missouri (-1.5, 41.5) Oklahoma has looked better since Witten took over. Quarterback John Mateer has settled down, and the offense is giving its defense a chance to rest. I understand why people would expect more points here. Against Ole Miss, all three of Oklahoma's offensive scoring drives took at least 12 plays, and Isaiah Sategna added a punt-return touchdown, which helped turn a game in which Mateer threw for 111 yards into a 24-17 win. Then against Texas A&M, the Sooners were tied entering the fourth quarter before finishing a 15-play touchdown drive that took more than eight minutes. A later interception set up a one-play touchdown to Sategna, making the final score look a lot more comfortable than the game had been. Witten can keep Mateer in manageable situations, use the running game and keep Missouri's offense off the field. Oklahoma's defense has held Florida and Texas A&M to seven points apiece during this stretch, with Ole Miss scoring 17 between them. Missouri will test it. QB Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes against Kentucky, and WR Donovan Olugbode caught two of them. I'm more concerned about those receivers creating quick scores than Missouri consistently driving the length of the field. The Tigers also allowed Kentucky into the red zone seven times while giving up only 14 points, so their defense gave up more chances than the final score suggests. I expect Oklahoma to stick with the patient approach that has worked under Witten, while making Simmons put together longer drives to score. Bet: Under 41.5 (-110) Minnesota at Wisconsin (-7.5, 37.5) Wisconsin just scored 42 points at Purdue, so this is a pretty low number to come back and bet under. RB Colton Joseph returned to the starting job and ran for 187 yards, including touchdowns from 32 and 66 yards out. Darrion Dupree broke a long touchdown run, too. Purdue couldn't handle the quarterback run game, and Wisconsin kept going back to it. Minnesota has to do a better job there. The Gophers allowed Northwestern to rush for 196 yards, and Joseph gave Wisconsin a way to turn a missed assignment into a touchdown without throwing the ball. That's the biggest concern with this bet — but I still don't trust Minnesota to score much. P.J. Fleck fired offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. after the Penn State loss, and Eric Koehler took over the play-calling against Northwestern. Darius Taylor ran the ball better and two missed field goals hurt, but the Gophers still went into halftime scoreless. Their first touchdown required a fourth-down conversion, and Anthony Smith then forced and recovered a fumble to give Minnesota a short field for its second TD. QB Drake Lindsey made a great throw late to set up the winning field goal, but even with those plays, Minnesota finished with only 20 points. It hasn't scored more than that in any of its past six games. I can give the coaching change some credit without expecting everything to be fixed before a trip to Wisconsin. The Badgers' defense ranks No. 21 in our ratings, and neither offense is in much of a hurry between snaps. If Minnesota can make Joseph and Dupree string together first downs instead of breaking long runs, Wisconsin can move the ball while taking plenty of time off the clock. Bet: Under 37.5 (-110) North Dakota State (-9.5, 39.5) at San José State San José State nearly forced overtime against UNLV, but the offense still had to work awfully hard to get to 22 points. QB Luke Weaver threw 40 passes while the Spartans ran for just 56 yards. They needed a late touchdown pass to Carson Clark to get within a 2-point conversion then couldn't complete the tying attempt. A week earlier, they scored three points at Air Force. We still rank this offense 128th, and I'm not convinced Weaver gets enough help from the running game to keep it moving against North Dakota State. The Bison's defense certainly gave us a reason to hesitate last week. They led Northern Illinois 31-3 before allowing touchdowns on the Huskies' final three possessions. I still put more weight on a defense we rank No. 29, which held Hawai'i to 13 points and UTEP to seven in its previous two games. San José State needs to sustain drives against that group, and its past two games haven't given me much confidence it can. QB Nathan Hayes is coming off a career-high four touchdown passes, but the Bison finished Saturday by adding defensive tackles as blockers and handing the ball to DJ Scott to run out the clock. With North Dakota State favored here, I expect it to lean on the running game if it gets ahead. I'll back its defense to keep San José State from turning this into a game Hayes has to win through the air. Bet: Under 39.5 (+100)

away.blurb: Oklahoma vs. Texas A&M injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners Skip to main content Recruiting OL Ryan Fodje: GAME-TIME DECISION Fodje injured his ankle in the loss to Kentucky and has been sidelined ever since. He was ruled out early in weeks until last week, when he was listed as doubtful before ultimately being unavailable against Ole Miss. He was questionable on Friday's report before becoming a game-time decision. Replacement: Although he's the starter at RG on the depth chart, Fodje could also replace E'Marion Harris at right tackle when he returns to the lineup. In the meantime, Heath Ozaeta has been anchoring that RG spot while Fodje has been out. Cornerback Dakoda Fields, who transferred from Oregon this offseason, has been out the last three games, and now, it's four after being listed as questionable until right before kickoff. RB Tory Blaylock: GAME-TIME DECISION Running back Tory Blaylock was also a game-time decision a week (and a day) ago before carrying the ball nine times for 48 yards, averaging 5.3 yards per carry. He's been a regular on the availability report after being banged up since before the season even kicked off, but he has still missed only the opener. He was listed as probable most of this week. Replacement: Freshman Jonathan Hatton Jr. will get touches whether Blaylock is available or not, but he should get even more if Blaylock is on the sidelines. We also had a brief Xavier Robinson sighting last week, so no Blaylock could help Robinson get on the field more. CB Dezz Ricks: game-time decision Everything seems to be going right for the Oklahoma Sooners right now, including a shrinking injury report. The No. 22 Sooners host Texas A&M on Saturday in Norman for a reunion between two old Big 12 rivals. OU, at 6-4, is eyeing a three-game winning streak and just appeared in the CFP rankings for the first time this season after back-to-back ranked wins. A lot of that newfound success is because of a change at offensive coordinator, with tight ends coach Jason Witten replacing Ben Arbuckle, but there's no doubt the Sooners getting healthier is also a major factor. It's not a long list, but there are still a few player statuses to keep an eye on before kickoff. This is the closest we've been in five weeks to seeing Ryan Fodje on the football field. If Fodje returns today, it would be the first time this season the Sooners have their full starting offensive line healthy. Before his injury, Fodje had started every game but the season opener, during which he was also injured. He's listed as the starter at right guard, but he hasn't actually played there yet this season. He filled in for Michael Fausi at left tackle for the five games he was healthy. My play is Washington +14. Ask a Ducks fan about the 2023 season and watch them wince. Washington beat Oregon twice that year, both by three points, and Dan Lanning's first three games against the Huskies were all three-point losses. Oregon has since won the last two meetings by double digits, and now it gets Washington at home on Senior Day with a Big Ten Championship Game trip on the line. Win, and the Ducks are in it in nearly every scenario. That's a lot of pressure to put on a two-touchdown number against a team that refuses to get blown out. The Huskies live in one-score games Washington's record is 7-4, but the résumé is better than that. Three of the four losses came by four points or fewer, and only Iowa beat them by more than four. Since quarterback Demond Williams Jr. came back from a fractured rib, the Huskies have been grinding out results, capped by last week's 27-24 overtime upset of then-No. 6 Indiana, the defending national champion. Williams is the reason this spread feels a touch rich. He broke a 65-yard touchdown run on the opening drive against Indiana and finished with 88 rushing yards to go with 227 through the air. He's one of only three Washington quarterbacks with 1,000 career rushing yards, so even when the pocket collapses he can turn a broken play into a first down. Former Duck Jayden Limar added 77 yards and a score in that game, and Washington piled up 189 on the ground. Washington's last five games at Michigan State The defense also has a knack for turning a game. Washington has 13 interceptions, seventh nationally per the school, with eight different Huskies picking one off. And punter Hunter Green leads the Big Ten at 47.1 yards per punt, which matters a lot when you're trying to keep a favorite from running away with field position. But this offense has had dry spells against real defenses. Oregon scored 15 in a home loss to UCLA, 17 in a three-point win over Nebraska and 10 in a loss at Illinois, all in October. Oregon also hasn't officially named its starter for Saturday, and running backs Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison were both less than full go on the last availability report. away.source: Hoosier State of Mind on MSN
away.blurb: A total of eight players appeared on Indiana's Week 12 availability report on Thursday night. Six of those players have already been ruled out for Saturday's contest against the Huskies, and that group includes some key starters. The biggest losses for Indiana come on the offensive side of the ball. RB Turbo Richard and OL Joe Brunner both being unavailable for the second straight week is a tough blow to Indiana's rushing attack. After taking down USC by a score of 27-13 last week, the Indiana Hoosiers are hitting the road in Week 12. Traveling across the country to Seattle, this weekend's tilt against Washington is the furthest road trip of the regular season for IU. For the most part, Indiana has stayed relatively healthy this season. Curt Cignetti has a solid strategy in place to keep his players healthy, which includes prioritizing player recovery, managing practice workloads, and ensuring athletes receive proper rest and conditioning throughout the season. But at the end of the day, this is still football and injuries happen. Heading into Week 12, the Hoosiers are dealing with some injuries to key players that present some challenges against Washington. Indiana Football Week 12 injury report Here's a look at the full availability report for Indiana heading into Week 12: Richard was brought in from Boston College over the offseason to be Indiana's RB1, and he thrived in that role when healthy. Richard has rushed for 745 yards and team-leading 6.6 yards per carry with 6 touchdowns this season. The good news is that Khobie Martin is back after missing the first half of the season with a broken forearm, and he rushed 12 times for 82 yards and a touchdown last week against USC. Lee Beebe Jr. has also been a reliable rushing force this season, and he totaled 71 yards on 16 carries last week against the Trojans. With Richard sidelined, Martin and Beebe figure to share the workload in the Hoosier backfield once again. Brunner is a fifth-year senior who has been a key part of Indiana's offensive line this season. He transferred to Indiana from Wisconsin back in the spring, and brought plenty of experience with him as he appeared in 39 games with 24 starts during his career with the Badgers. Owning a 6'7" 320-pound frame, Brunner started the first nine games of the season at right guard for the Hoosiers. In his absence, redshirt sophomore Austin Liebfried got the starting nod at right guard against USC on Saturday afternoon. He could be expected to continue in that role, but freshman Sam Simpson could also see expanded opportunities. Last week without Richard and Brunner, Indiana ran for 146 yards and 4.2 yards per carry against USC. Washington's run defense isn't the best in the world, as the Huskies rank 10th in the Big Ten by allowing 132.4 rushing yards per game to their opponents. home.blurb: Milivojevic is one of 10 Spartans listed out on the Big Ten availability report, with seven more listed questionable, according to Connor Earegood of The Detroit News . It is the second game Milivojevic has missed this season. Backup Cam Fancher is listed as questionable with a knee injury. If Fancher cannot go, true freshman Kayd Coffman is in line for the start. Coffman has already made a start this season and has completed 4 of 11 passes for 42 yards with one touchdown and one interception, per ESPN's team statistics . Who else is out for the Spartans on Senior Night Beyond Milivojevic, Michigan State lists defensive tackle Ben Roberts, safety Devin Vaught, linebacker Jordan Hall, running back Marvis Parrish, tight end Jayden Savoury, running back Cam Edwards, fullback Jay Coyne, offensive lineman Tristan Comer and tight end Joe Caudill as out, per Chris Solari of the Detroit Free Press . Alongside Fancher, the questionable list carries left guard Conner Moore, tight end Brennan Parachek, safety Michael Richard, running back Jaziun Patterson, receiver Rodney Bullard Jr. and cornerback Tre Bell. That is a thin roster for a team that has already been eliminated from bowl contention and is playing for its seniors. Dante Moore, the Detroit King product who opened the season as Oregon's starter, has not played since September and is out again on Friday. Ducks coach Dan Lanning said this week that he does not anticipate Moore playing again this season, according to Athlon Sports . Dylan Raiola has carried the offense since, completing 141 of 213 passes for 1,695 yards with 15 touchdowns and two interceptions, per ESPN . Oregon lists nine players out in all: Moore, running back Jordon Davison, receiver Iverson Hooks, defensive back Aaron Flowers, inside linebacker Brayden Platt, outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti, defensive lineman Matthew Johnson and offensive linemen Trent Ferguson and Dave Iuli. picks.headline: Four Bold Predictions for Oklahoma State Cowboys vs. Arizona State Sun Devils in Week 12
picks.blurb: Four Bold Predictions for Oklahoma State Cowboys vs. Arizona State Sun Devils in Week 12 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Steelers release Aaron Rodgers Latest CFP rankings MLB free agency updates NBA Cup roundup Viral Ga. Tech couple Oklahoma State Cowboys head coach Eric Morris. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Matt Postins · Oklahoma State Cowboys On SI Fri, November 20, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Earlier this week Oklahoma State head coach Eric Morris made it clear his team has something to play for even with the Big 12 title game off the table. He didn't want to hear anything about lower intensity from his Cowboys (6-4, 4-3 in Big 12) as they prepared for a 9:15 p.m. central kickoff against Arizona State (6-4, 4-3) on Saturday. "[That's] such a silly question to ask - what is there left to play? For us, right now, it's building this thing up, and for our players that have fought so hard [finishing this season is important]." The Cowboys are bowl eligible for the first time since 2023. The Sun Devils are bowl eligible for the third year in a row. The winner of this game could end up with a better bowl bid with a victory. As the Cowboys prepare for a late kickoff against the Sun Devils, here are four bold predictions, including the final score. Caleb Hawkins Has 200+ Yards in Total Offense Oklahoma State Cowboys running back Caleb Hawkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Arizona State's defense has been better the past few weeks. It's part of the reason the Sun Devils have won three of their last four games. In that span, they've given up fewer than 17 points three times and allowed 27 points to BYU in the one loss. Arizona State has figured some things out and Morris noted that the Sun Devils have stopped the run well of late. The Cowboys have featured Caleb Hawkins in a big way the last five games. He's rushed for 648 yards and five touchdowns and caught 32 passes for 401 yards and three touchdowns. That's 1,049 all-purpose yards in five games. He's second in the country in the category. Oklahoma State wants to feature him. More important, given Drew Mestemaker's shoulder injury, the Cowboys NEED to feature him. He got 26 touches against Texas Tech and had 143 yards without a score. I suspect the Cowboys are going to feed him in the run game early to allow Mestemaker to settle in - I expected him to start - and then get him the ball in space in the pass game once Mestemaker is comfortably. The Cowboys need him to get 200 or more yards in total offense on Saturday. I think he gets it. Broderick Vehrs Plays a Role on Offense Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Broderick Vehrs. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As I just wrote, I expect Drew Mestemaker to start at quarterback. But it doesn't mean that head coach Eric Morris can't use Broderick Vehrs in some way. He's likely gotten some first-team reps this week on the off-chance that Mestemaker can't go. That has given Morris a chance to look at ways to use the true freshman in ways that could lessen Mestemaker's load and reduce his exposure to injury. Morris has gotten creative with the playbook at times. A couple of weeks ago he ran a play-action shovel pass that happened so quickly I'm not sure anyone realized it. There is little Morris can do if Mestemaker gets flushed out of the pocket. But he won't want to use Mestemaker in designed runs. That's where Vehrs can come in handy. He's shown an ability to run the ball in RPO looks that could help throw defenses off in the right circumstance. He has 58 yards rushing on just five carries so there is some explosiveness there. How Morris uses Vehrs will depend on comfort level. But a package that allows him a handful of plays to try and throw off Arizona State's defense would have the added benefit of minimizing Mestemaker's exposure to re-injury. The Cowboys Get a Defensive Touchdown OSU safety Evan Jackson. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect It's time. In fact, it's past time for the Oklahoma State Cowboys to land another defensive touchdown. It's Game 11. It's time for someone to find the end zone the same way safety Evan Jackson did against UCF. Why should the offense have all the fun? But why this week? The Sun Devils moved to true freshman quarterback Jake Fette as the starter three games ago and he's had a similar impact on Arizona State as veteran quarterback Thomas Castelllanos has had on Texas Tech. He's thrown for 623 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He's also rushed for 23 yards. He hasn't committed a turnover ... yet. Fette will be without one of his top wide receivers, Omarion Miller, who has caught 49 passes this season. He played last week against UCF, so Fette hasn't had the chance to play without the team's second-highest producing receiver. That takes away a rock-solid target. The Cowboys will also be looking for redemption defensively after giving up 52 points to the Red Raiders. Remember how Oklahoma State answered after giving up 51 points to Iowa State? The Cowboys allowed 28 points to Kansas State and forced three turnovers. That's the kind of bounce-back I'm expecting from the Cowboys this Saturday. That bounce-back will lead to a turnover that leads to a defensive touchdown. Given his hard work the past two months, I'll take the easy way out and say LaDainian Fields ends up with a pick-six. Score Prediction Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Drew Mestemaker. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Oklahoma State 37, Arizona State 33 The Cowboys haven't been great on the road this season. The performances have been uneven and they're 2-3 away from BPS. But Oklahoma State has followed up every loss with a win this season and I think that's what happens on Saturday. I think quarterback Drew Mestemaker plays without restrictions, but that running back Caleb Hawkins ends up being the star of the show. The defense frustrates ASU quarterback Jake Fette just enough to force him into his first significant mistakes of the season. Cowboys kicker Sam Keltner boots a career-long field goal in the thinner air of Tempe. After that, Oklahoma State will fly home for the regular-season finale against Kansas and awaits its bowl game invitation. home.blurb: STILLWATER — Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker is listed as questionable on OSU's initial availability report Wednesday night for the Cowboys' road game against Arizona State . Tight end Carson Kolb, defensive tackle Landon Dean and receiver Dayvon Standard are listed as out for Saturday's road game against the Sun Devils. Linebacker Tate Romney and offensive lineman Desmond Magiya are listed as doubtful. Tight end Morgan McPhaul is listed as questionable. Linebacker Ethan Wesloski is listed as probable. Arizona State safety Adrian Wilson crashed into Coleman, sending the 5-foot-6, 158-pound receiver toppling over. Medical personnel walked Coleman into the injury tent, where he remained for the remainder of the drive. The play was reviewed for targeting and upheld. Wilson is ejected from the game. Deion Imade on the Cowboy Radio Network reported Coleman emerged from the tent with a smile on his face and was attempting to convince OSU personnel he is able to continue playing. Coleman leads OSU against Arizona State with four receptions for 46 yards. OSU trails Arizona State 24-14 with 10:39 remaining in the third quarter.
